Pretty normal stuff. Being about 3 or 4 years old, I was not particularly skilled in the way of social interaction or personal boundaries. As you can imagine, that led to me saying some things that would have best been left unsaid. My favorite one is this:

I was sitting in the of the shopping cart while in the checkout line. There was a large, tan man checking out his things in front of us. When he turned to put his stuff on the conveyor belt, I got a full look at him. He was "round," fairly dark, wore flowery swim trunks, and a tank top. He also had a bandanna on his head and an eyepatch.

Young me was entranced. This was completely outlandish to me; I hadn't seen a pirate in a supermarket before!

"Stop staring," said my mother, quietly.

I did not stop.

"Stop staring!" she said, more sternly.

I couldn't help myself. I wanted to talk to him in a way he'd understand. I looked at him right in the eye.

"Arr, matey!" I blurted.

My mom gasped, but the man just let out a huge laugh, right from the belly. She was incredibly apologetic and embarrassed, but the "pirate" couldn't care less. She checked out as fast as she could and pretty much ran out the door. I had a big smile on my face. I just got to talk to a real pirate, I thought.

She laughs about it now, but I can only imagine how flustered my mom was at the time.
